The remilitarisation of the Rhineland ( German : Rheinlandbesetzung , pronounced [ˈʁaɪnlantˌbəˈzɛtsʊŋ] ) began on 7 March 1936, when military forces of Nazi Germany entered the Rhineland , which directly contravened the Treaty of Versailles and the Locarno Treaties . Neither France nor Britain was prepared for a military response, so they did not act. After 1939, commentators often said that a strong military move in 1936 might have ruined the expansionist plans of Adolf Hitler , the dictator of Germany. However, recent historiography agrees that both public and elite opinion in Britain and France strongly opposed a military intervention, and neither had an army prepared to move in. [ 1 ]
